description: `flushSync(fn)` from `react-dom` applies the updates inside `fn` synchronously, so the DOM is current when it returns.
Since React 18, all updates in the same tick (events, timeouts, promises) are batched into one render.
Right after calling a setter, the DOM still reflects the previous render.
An API for rare imperative needs. flushSync opts out of batching and can hurt performance.
